_README: SDI's prices, as DATA — reviewable and changeable without a code edit.
Every entry is one price. `amount` is the money; everything beside it is what an
estimator needs to decide whether to trust it: where it came from, when that source
was current, what it may price, how firm it is, and when it should be looked at again.
WHAT MAY ENTER THIS FILE — James Gray, 16 Sep 2026:
'A number copied from an estimator's sheet is not a price source, even as a
reference. It must not be retained in the current register, documentation,
reports, prompts, tests, or audit payloads.'
'Unless there is a re-useable / understandable calculation we can't use it.'
So an entry needs a CURRENT, REPRODUCIBLE source: an SDI Live / UDEF lookup, a
supplier catalogue or API, or an identified quote document for the job in hand.
A figure relayed off a manual estimate — however honestly attributed — does not
qualify and is not kept here in any status. What carries forward from old estimates
is the METHOD: item identity, specification, route, applicability and evidence,
which live in config and the change register, number-free.
status:  live       a current system/supplier price — the engine may charge it
confirmed  a current quote or figure confirmed for its scope
indicative a market/derived figure — priced, labelled, to be replaced
scope:   material / department / customer / job_family / job_only. `job_only` prices
that job and nothing else.
review_date is not decoration. Past it, the engine keeps pricing — silence is worse —
and says the figure is out of review so nobody mistakes age for agreement.
This file is empty because nothing SDI holds today meets the standard. A line the
engine cannot price from SDI Live or a current supplier source is raised AWAITING
PRICE, naming what is missing and who owns it — never filled from a sheet.
